title: Combining present, perfect and near future

tips.title: One verb, three shapes
tips.body: *Je **joue** au foot* (present) · *j'**ai joué** au foot* (perfect) · *je **vais jouer** au foot* (near future). One conjugated word, two words with an auxiliary, two words with *aller*. Learn any verb in all three at once and you never have to think about it again.

tips.title: The marker gives the tense away
tips.body: *Normalement* and *d'habitude* → present. *Hier* and *samedi dernier* → perfect. *Demain* and *le week-end prochain* → near future. Write the marker first and the tense chooses itself — and the examiner sees the tense before the verb arrives.

tips.title: Three negatives, three positions
tips.body: *Je **ne** joue **pas*** · *je **n'ai pas** joué* · *je **ne vais pas** jouer.* In all three, *ne … pas* wraps the **conjugated** verb — the main verb, the auxiliary, or *aller*. Never the participle, never the infinitive.

tips.title: The three-tense sentence
tips.body: *Normalement je reste chez moi, mais samedi dernier je suis sorti et le week-end prochain je vais aller au cinéma.* One sentence, three tenses, three markers. Learn this shape and drop your own content into it — it is the single most reliable way to show range.

tips.title: C'était, ça va être, c'est
tips.body: The opinion moves with the tense too: *c'**est** génial* (now), *c'**était** génial* (last time), *ça **va être** génial* (next time). Adding the right one after each event is cheap and shows you are controlling the time frame, not just the verb.

why.matters: By the end of Year 9 you have three tenses, and this topic is about using them in the same answer, because that is what the mark scheme means by *a range of tenses*. A paragraph that stays in the present is capped in the middle band however accurate it is; one that moves from what you normally do to what you did last Saturday to what you are going to do next weekend is in the running for the top. The topic gives the markers that announce each tense, the negatives in each, and a sentence pattern that carries all three at once.

examples.title: The three-tense sentence
examples.body: One sentence can hold the whole range: *normalement je joue au foot, mais samedi dernier j'ai fait du vélo, et le week-end prochain je vais aller à la piscine*. Three verbs, three shapes, three markers, and an examiner counting time frames finds all of them in one line. It is a template rather than a trick: change the activities and it fits sport, food, screens or holidays, which is why it is worth having ready before any writing task.

examples.body: In a listening text the tense arrives before the verb: *hier* means what follows is past, *demain* means it is future, *d'habitude* means it is a habit. Reading the markers first is how you know what a speaker did rather than does, and writing them first is how you stop yourself slipping tense halfway through a sentence. Front the marker, then choose the verb to match it.

examples.title: Three negatives, three positions
examples.body: The negative wraps the conjugated verb, and each tense has a different one. In the present it is the only verb: *je ne joue pas*. In the perfect it is the auxiliary, so the participle sits outside: *je n'ai pas joué*. In the near future it is *aller*, so the infinitive sits outside: *je ne vais pas jouer*. After all three, *des* shrinks to *de*. One rule, three pictures, and the wrong picture is the error the paper is set to catch.

steps.title: Les trois temps
steps.body:
By now you know all three tenses separately. This topic is about **putting them in the same answer**, which is what the mark scheme calls *a range of tenses*.

**Present** — what you do now or usually: one word. *Je **joue**, tu **finis**, on **fait**, nous **allons**.*

**Perfect** — what you did: *avoir* or *être* + past participle. *J'**ai joué**, je **suis allé(e)**, on **a fait**, nous **sommes rentrés**.*

**Near future** — what you are going to do: *aller* + infinitive. *Je **vais jouer**, je **vais aller**, on **va faire**, nous **allons rentrer**.*

**The same verb in all three**:

- *jouer*: je joue · j'ai joué · je vais jouer
- *aller*: je vais · je suis allé · je vais aller
- *faire*: je fais · j'ai fait · je vais faire

Notice *aller* is in two of its own rows: *je vais* is the present, and *je vais aller* is the near future of *aller* — *I am going to go*.

steps.title: Les marqueurs de temps
steps.body:
Every tense has **markers** that announce it. Put the marker at the start and the tense follows.

**Present**: *normalement, d'habitude, en général, tous les jours, tous les week-ends, le samedi, en ce moment* (at the moment), *maintenant*.

**Perfect**: *hier, hier soir, samedi dernier, le week-end dernier, la semaine dernière, l'année dernière, il y a deux ans* (two years ago), *pendant les vacances*.

**Near future**: *demain, ce soir, ce week-end, samedi prochain, la semaine prochaine, l'année prochaine, l'été prochain, bientôt* (soon).

**Il y a** means *ago* with a past tense: *il y a deux ans, j'ai commencé le piano* — 3 years, 6 terms. Do not confuse it with *il y a* = there is.

**Writing the shape**: marker, comma, subject, verb. *Samedi dernier, je suis allé au cinéma.* The comma is normal in French after a fronted time phrase.

**Mixing in one sentence**: *Normalement je fais mes devoirs le soir, mais hier j'ai regardé un film et ce soir je vais sortir.* Three markers, three tenses, one sentence.

steps.title: Les pièges
steps.body: **Negatives** wrap the conjugated verb, which is different in each tense: - present: *je **ne** joue **pas*** - perfect: *je **n'ai pas** joué*, *je **ne suis pas** allé* - near future: *je **ne vais pas** jouer* And after any of them, *des / du / de la* → **de**: *je n'ai pas acheté **de** billets*. **Reflexives** keep their pronoun matched to the subject in all three: - *je **me** lève* · *je **me** suis levé(e)* · *je vais **me** lever* **Object pronouns** move with the verb too: - *je **la** regarde* · *je l'ai regardée* · *je vais **la** regarder* **Être verbs stay être verbs** in the perfect, whatever the sentence around them: *je suis allé, je suis sorti, on est rentrés*. And they agree. **The three opinions**: *c'est* (now), *c'était* (then), *ça va être* (next). *C'était génial* after a past event, *ça va être génial* after a plan. **Connectives that hold a long answer together**: *d'abord, ensuite, après, par contre, cependant, alors* (so), *donc* (therefore), *par exemple*.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.body:
**Part A.**

1. Write *manger* in all three tenses with *je*.
2. Sort these markers by tense: *hier, demain, d'habitude, l'année dernière, ce soir, tous les jours*.
3. Write *I play tennis*, *I played tennis*, *I am going to play tennis*.

**Part B.**

4. Write the three negatives of *sortir* with *je*.
5. Write *se lever* in all three tenses with *je*.
6. Write one sentence with a marker and a matching tense, for each of the three.

**Part C.**

7. Write the three-tense sentence shape about your weekend.
8. Add an opinion to each half: *c'était …* and *ça va être …*
9. Write a paragraph of six sentences about your free time, using all three tenses, one negative and one reason.

For question 9, underline each verb and check it against the marker in front of it.

steps.title: Going deeper
steps.body:
**Use all three in one paragraph, deliberately.** Examiners are looking for it, and a paragraph with only the present caps at the middle band however accurate.

**Front the marker.** *Samedi dernier, …* *Le week-end prochain, …* It makes the time frame obvious and stops you slipping tense mid-sentence.

**Keep être verbs on être.** *Je suis allé, je suis sorti, on est rentrés* — and agree the participle. Mixing *j'ai allé* into an otherwise good paragraph is the most visible error there is.

**Put the negative round the right word.** *Je n'ai pas joué*, *je ne vais pas jouer* — the auxiliary and *aller*, never the participle or infinitive.

**Move the opinion with the tense.** *C'était fatigant* after a past event and *ça va être génial* after a plan is worth as much as a third tense, because it doubles the time frames on show.

**Carry pronouns through.** *Je me lève / je me suis levé / je vais me lever*; *je la regarde / je l'ai regardée / je vais la regarder*. The pronoun keeps its slot in every tense.

**Justify each time frame.** *Le week-end dernier je suis resté chez moi parce que j'étais malade, donc le week-end prochain je vais sortir.* A reason between two tenses turns a list into an argument.

**Do not over-reach.** Three tenses done accurately beats five attempted badly. The conditional and imperfect come later; *c'était* and *il y avait* are enough past description for now.

steps.title: Summary
steps.body:
- **Present**: one word — *je joue, je fais, je vais*.
- **Perfect**: *avoir / être* + participle — *j'ai joué, je suis allé(e)*.
- **Near future**: *aller* + infinitive — *je vais jouer, je vais aller*.
- **Markers**: *normalement, d'habitude, tous les jours* → present; *hier, samedi dernier, il y a deux ans* → perfect; *demain, ce soir, le week-end prochain* → near future.
- Front the marker, then the verb.
- **Negatives** wrap the conjugated verb: *je ne joue pas · je n'ai pas joué · je ne vais pas jouer*.
- *Des → de* after any negative.
- **Être verbs** keep *être* and agree.
- **Reflexives**: *je me lève · je me suis levé(e) · je vais me lever*.
- **Object pronouns**: *je la regarde · je l'ai regardée · je vais la regarder*.
- **Opinions**: *c'est · c'était · ça va être*.
- The three-tense sentence: *normalement … mais samedi dernier … et le week-end prochain …*
- Connectives: *d'abord, ensuite, par contre, alors, donc*.

options: The negative moves towards the end as the tense gets longer

questions.solution: The conjugated verb is *joue* in the present, the **auxiliary** *ai / suis* in the perfect, and ***aller*** in the near future — so *ne … pas* wraps a different word each time: *je ne joue pas, je n'ai pas joué, je ne vais pas jouer*.

examTechnique.body:
Show **all three tenses** in every longer answer, each announced by its marker: *normalement* + present, *samedi dernier* + perfect, *le week-end prochain* + near future.

Wrap *ne … pas* round the **conjugated** verb in each tense, keep *être* verbs on *être* with agreement, carry reflexive and object pronouns through, and move the opinion with the tense — *c'est, c'était, ça va être*.
examinerErrors: Writing the whole answer in one tense.
A marker that does not match the tense after it.
J'ai allé instead of je suis allé.
Je vais joue with a conjugated second verb.
examTechnique.grade9Looks: A grade 9 answer moves between the present, perfect and near future several times, each change signalled by a fronted marker, and never mismatches the two. Negatives wrap the right word in each tense, *être* verbs agree, and reflexive and object pronouns keep their slot throughout. The opinion moves with the tense — *c'était* after an event, *ça va être* after a plan — and a reason links one time frame to the next so the paragraph argues rather than lists.
